title: Tech Note: Building Interactive Graphic Interfaces with 4D Draw, Part 1
author: Tim Tonooka

historical_commentary.text: This extensive Tech Note is a remarkable artifact of late-1990s 4D development, demonstrating how developers built sophisticated interactive graphical interfaces using 4D Draw—a plug-in that has since been completely discontinued. The detailed comparison of 4D Draw vs. 4D Chart, the manual BMP file parsing via BLOB operations, and the bitmap-to-vector tracing algorithm written entirely in 4D code showcase the ingenuity required before modern image libraries and SVG support existed. The references to ACI_Pack, PICT format, QuickDraw, and classic Mac/Windows graphics programs like Adobe Streamline and CorelTrace place this firmly in its era.
related_updates: 4D Draw has been discontinued and removed from the 4D product line
ACI_Pack plug-in is no longer available
PICT format and QuickDraw are deprecated Apple technologies
Modern 4D supports SVG natively and provides Web Areas for interactive graphics
